name: Animals
facts: An octopus has three hearts: two pump blood through the gills and one pumps it to the rest of the body.
Cats spend roughly two-thirds of their lives asleep.
A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
Elephants can communicate using low rumbles that travel several kilometres through the ground.
Koalas sleep up to 20 hours a day, partly because their eucalyptus diet gives them very little energy.
Snails can seal themselves inside their shells and stay dormant for months to survive dry weather.
Elephants are among the few animals that can recognise themselves in a mirror.
Sloths can hold their breath for up to 40 minutes, longer than dolphins.
Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings.
A hummingbird's heart can beat more than 1,200 times a minute.
Sea otters hold hands while sleeping so they don't drift apart.
Crows can recognise individual human faces and remember people who treated them badly.
The cheetah is the fastest land animal, reaching speeds of around 100 km/h in short bursts.
Giraffes have the same number of neck bones as humans: seven.
Honeybees communicate the location of flowers with a 'waggle dance'.
Penguins only live in the Southern Hemisphere (in the wild).
A shrimp's heart is located in its head.
Dogs' nose prints are unique, much like human fingerprints.
Butterflies taste with their feet.
Owls can't move their eyes, so they turn their heads up to about 270 degrees instead.
Starfish don't have blood; they use seawater to move nutrients around their bodies.
A blue whale's tongue can weigh as much as an elephant.
Rats make ultrasonic chirps when tickled, a sound researchers compare to laughter.
Polar bears have black skin under their white-looking fur.
Some species of tortoise can live for more than 150 years.
